company.name: Taskhive
company.description: Project management for agencies. Support gets weekly tickets from admins confused by the settings page.

title: Taskhive: the settings page
brief: This is the settings page of Taskhive, as it ships today. Use it like a customer would, then mark every usability problem you find: click the part of the screen, name the problem and say what you saw. Some parts are fine, and flagging them counts against you.

issues.explanation: The page title is smaller than the section headings below it, so the structure reads upside down and nothing anchors where you are.
issues.fix: Keep a clear scale: page title largest, then section headings, then labels.

issues.explanation: The profile fields are filled in but have no labels, so you cannot tell which value is which field, especially when one is empty.
issues.fix: Give every field a visible label.

issues.explanation: The only button on a long settings page says 'OK'. It does not say that it saves, so people leave without saving, or press it expecting to close something.
issues.fix: Label the button with its action: 'Save changes'.

issues.explanation: Deleting the whole workspace is a big, brand-colored button that looks like the main action and works on a single click, with no confirmation and no undo.
issues.fix: Put irreversible actions in a separate danger zone, style them as destructive, and ask for confirmation (e.g. typing the workspace name).

hidden.principle: Judge a screen by the user's goal: every element should help them reach it, say clearly what will happen, and tell them what did happen.

toggles: Email me when I am assigned a task

props.text: Notification changes apply to every workspace you belong to.

userGoal: A Taskhive admin wants to update their profile, choose which notifications they get and check their plan.
